record.paper_title: Syzygies of projective varieties of large degree: recent progress and open problems.
record.context_brief: weight-one curve syzygies for large degree
record.original_question: Let C be a smooth projective curve, let B be a line bundle on C, and let L_d be a line bundle of sufficiently large degree. For exactly which integers p is the weight-one Koszul cohomology group K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d) nonzero? The source later answers this by showing that K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d) vanishes for all sufficiently large d if and only if B is p-very ample, which resolves the question in the source artifact.

evidence.quote: However this leaves open the Question 4.1. For which values of p is Kp,1(C,B ;Ld) ̸= 0 when d ≫ 0?
Theorem 4.3. Fix a line bundle B on C. Then Kp,1(C,B ;Ld) = 0 for d ≫ 0 if and only if B is p-very ample.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, and let $B$ be a line bundle on $C$. For each integer $d$, let $L_d$ be a line bundle on $C$ of degree $d$, and consider the section ring \[ R(C,B;L_d) \;=\; \bigoplus_{q\ge 0} H^0\!\bigl(C,\,B\otimes L_d^{\otimes q}\bigr), \] viewed as a graded module over the section ring $S(L_d)=\bigoplus_q H^0(C,L_d^{\otimes q})$. For integers $p\ge 0$ and $q\ge 0$, let $K_{p,q}(C,B;L_d)$ denote the Koszul cohomology group computed as the cohomology at the middle term of \[ \wedge^{p+1}H^0(L_d)\otimes H^0(B\otimes L_d^{q-1}) \to \wedge^{p}H^0(L_d)\otimes H^0(B\otimes L_d^{q}) \to \wedge^{p-1}H^0(L_d)\otimes H^0(B\otimes L_d^{q+1}). \] Recall that a line bundle $B$ on $C$ is said to be $p$-very ample if for every effective divisor $\xi$ of degree $p+1$ on $C$ the restriction map $H^0(C,B)\to H^0(C,B\otimes\mathcal{O}_\xi)$ is surjective.

Determine, in terms of $B$, exactly which nonnegative integers $p$ have the property that \[ K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d)\;\neq\;0 \quad\text{for all sufficiently large } d. \] Equivalently, characterize those $p$ for which $K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d)$ vanishes for $d\gg 0$.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of characterizing nonvanishing of weight-one Koszul cohomology $K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d)$ for $d\gg 0$ has been answered: $K_{p,1}(C,B;L_d)=0$ for $d\gg 0$ if and only if $B$ is $p$-very ample. This is the Ein–Lazarsfeld vanishing/nonvanishing theorem for syzygies of curves of large degree, and is recorded as a theorem in the surveys on syzygies of varieties of large degree.
